execution_steps: 1. Surveyed ora's remaining 20 unresolved obligations by capability cluster; found 7 sharing a composite-op registry gap (6 with identical rule_text, 1 -- SAL-ORA-OBL-071A5F40BB2F4A17 -- with a distinct bundled 'reject invalid values' rule_text left untouched this tick, since the spec's own extensibility statement makes blanket rejection of unrecognized composite-op values spec-nonconformant, a genuinely separate question deferred to avoid conflating two different findings).

2. Located the pinned, authority-locked spec source cited by these obligations' authority_source_ids (SRC-ORA-003): .local/format-contracts/acquired/ora/src-ora-003.bin, the Layer Stack Specification. Read the 'composite-op attribute' section directly, extracting its own HTML table (20 rows: Value / Blending function / Compositing Operator) plus the immediately following prose confirming the default (svg:src-over) and the deliberate open-vocabulary design ('In the future other compositing modes might be added...').

3. Wrote a new module, composite_ops.py, transcribing the table's 20 entries into a CompositeOpInfo(blending_function, compositing_operator) registry plus a composite_op_info() lookup returning None for unrecognized values -- grounded entirely in the just-read spec text, not memory.

4. Refactored stack.py's existing DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_OP constant to import from the new module (single source of truth, no duplicated literal) and added a composite_op_details property to OraNode (inherited by OraLayer/OraStack/OraText) wired to the new lookup.
5. Wired the new symbols through model/__init__.py and the top-level ora/__init__.py, matching the existing top-level-import convention every ora test file already uses.

6. Ran an interactive probe before writing any formal test: default/multiply/unknown-value/stack lookups all matched expectations on the first attempt, including the forward-compatibility case (an unrecognized value returns None without raising, and the raw string survives unchanged on the node).

7. Wrote 11 tests: registry completeness, default-value mapping, a blend-only case, a Porter-Duff-operator-only case, the one non-Source-Over-operator case (svg:plus -> Lighter), the unrecognized-value-returns-None case, OraLayer/OraStack accessor wiring, a behavioral forward-compat preservation proof, and an exhaustive round-trip over all 20 registry entries.

8. Ran ruff (clean) across all 4 changed/new source files plus the new test file. Ran the full ora suite (305 passed, was 294, +11) and the full 6-format regression (3107 passed, was 3096, +11; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

9. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-daad05d457a5bc7c, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
